title: $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ at $T=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a scheme over $k$ and $\sigma\in X(k)$. Then

$$
\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(k)=\operatorname{Pic}(X)
$$

canonically.

proof.text: For $T=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$, the canonical base-change identifications give $X_T=X$ and $\sigma_T=\sigma:\operatorname{Spec}(k)\to X$. By [def-pc-pic-sigma-functor], $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(k)$ is the kernel of $\sigma^*: \operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Pic}(\operatorname{Spec} k)$. For every invertible module $\mathcal L$ on $X$, $\sigma^*\mathcal L$ is an invertible module on $\operatorname{Spec}(k)$, hence trivial by [lem-pc-pic-of-field]; no closed-immersion hypothesis is needed. Thus the map is zero and its kernel is all of $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$.
